To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GNO is a ferromagnetic material with a Curie temperature of ∼ 50 K and the co-existence phenomenon of different magnetic phases is explained by a combined formula.

GNO exhibits ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism and paramagnetism in a temperature range of 4–300 K, and the combined formula generated from 3D spin wave model and the Johnston formula successfully explains the magnetic behavior of the GNO.
the combined formula successfully describes the co-existence and contribution of ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic and paramagnetic phases at different temperatures.

the synthesis of GNO, its structural and magnetic properties.
the structural and magnetic properties of nanocrystalline Gd1.9Ni0.10 O3−δ synthesized by a simple chemical route.
a comprehensive investigation of microstructure and magnetism of Gd1.9Ni0.10 O3−δ nanocrystals synthesized by co- precipitation method.

the co-existence and dominance of different magnetic phases at different temperatures in the GNO sample is due to the presence of Ni2+ and Ni4+ ions, oxygen vacancies and F-centers.
the ferromagnetism is dominated by FCE coupling, which is mediated by the oxygen vacancy.
